structure:
repos/trade-imports-ins-backend is a small Java / Spring Boot service (about 100 files). It consumes notification outbox events from an SQS queue and upserts them into a Mongo 'notifications' collection (the cross-journey read model), then serves that read model read-only at GET /notifications. The read model lives in one package, src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/ins/backend/notification/ (10 classes, about 470 lines: the AggregatedNotification document with fields aggregateId, aggregateVersion, referenceNumber, status, originCountry, commodity, arrivalDate, lastUpdated; the controller with page, sort and referenceNumber parameters; the query service, sort parser, page response, repository; the SQS listener, upsert service, outbox event types and error handler), with its unit tests (7 files, about 750 lines) and integration tests AggregatedNotificationControllerIT and NotificationSqsListenerIT (about 300 lines), plus GlobalExceptionHandler (174 lines), application.yml (160 lines), compose/mongo/10-init.js and the README (108 lines). No rulings ledger exists in the repo. The scope (the read model behind the dashboard: fields, statuses, filters, sort and search) is about 2,000 lines, so it is one part. Left out: the addresslookup package (postcode address lookup proxy, 12 classes and 7 tests), which is not the dashboard read model; platform config (TLS, proxy, AWS, metrics, logging, tracing filters and interceptors, health check) and their tests; CI workflows, Dockerfile, floci and compose plumbing other than the Mongo init script.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Notification read model and dashboard query API: Part 1 of 1, read at repos/trade-imports-ins-backend HEAD 8c87fc97 (main, 5 Oct 2026). Read in full: README.md (still the CDP Java backend template text, nothing service-specific); the workspace page docs/repos/trade-imports-ins-backend.md; all 12 classes of src/main/java/.../notification (AggregatedNotification document, AggregatedNotificationController, AggregatedNotificationQueryService, AggregatedNotificationSort, AggregatedNotificationPageResponse, AggregatedNotificationRepository, NotificationSqsListener, NotificationUpsertService, OutboxEventType, NotificationErrorHandler, SqsRetryableException, SqsNonRetryableException); exceptions/GlobalExceptionHandler, NotFoundException, ConflictException; src/main/resources/application.yml; compose/mongo/10-init.js (a template comment only, seeds nothing); and the 10 test files the partition names (7 notification unit tests, GlobalExceptionHandlerTest, and the Testcontainers ITs AggregatedNotificationControllerIT and NotificationSqsListenerIT). One extra grep of src/main confirmed which exception classes are ever thrown and where the SQS error handler is wired (configuration/AwsConfig.java, not otherwise read). Covered, in this order: the read-model record (8 fields, the 'notifications' collection, its two indexes, the event-body path each field is filled from); status values and the DELETED exclusion; GET /notifications (page, sort, referenceNumber, page size 25, the six page-response fields, validation); every sort option, its default, malformed and unknown values, and the absence of a tie-breaker; reference-number search (trimmed, exact, single result, page 1 of 1, empty not 404) and the absence of any other filter or free-text search; event ingestion (8 accepted event types, message checks, field mapping, the aggregateVersion guard, partial updates, retryable versus discarded errors, metrics); the error responses GlobalExceptionHandler can give; the absence of user or organisation scoping and of authentication on the endpoint; notification configuration (queue, page size, Mongo read and write settings, API docs off); and what each unit and integration test proves. No rulings ledger exists in the repo.

claims.quote: // Single atomic operation: only applies when the stored version is lower than the incoming // version. Concurrent events for the same notification and out-of-order redelivery both // converge to the highest applied version without a read-then-write race.

claims.statement: The first event for a notification creates its record, whatever its event type.
claims.quote: Update update = new Update() .setOnInsert("_id", aggregateId) ... mongoTemplate.upsert(query, update, AggregatedNotification.class);

claims.statement: An event with a version equal to or lower than the stored one changes nothing, but it is likely to surface as a database duplicate-key error that the error handler then counts and logs as a discarded error, not as a quiet skip.
claims.quote: Query query = Query.query( Criteria.where("_id").is(aggregateId) .and(AGGREGATE_VERSION).lt(incomingVersion)); mongoTemplate.upsert(query, update, AggregatedNotification.class);
claims.note: When the version filter matches nothing, an upsert tries to insert a record with the same _id, which Mongo refuses. The ITs prove the stored version is kept but do not check the error metric or log.

claims.statement: Errors are split into retryable ones, which are left on the queue for SQS to redeliver, and all others, which are discarded and the message deleted.
claims.quote: log.warn("Retryable error, message left for retry: {}", ...); throw retryableException; } discardedCounter.increment(); log.error("Non-retryable error, message will be deleted: {}", ...

claims.statement: An unclassified error, such as a database failure, is treated as non-retryable: the message is deleted and not retried.

claims.statement: Nothing in the service ever raises a retryable error, so in practice every failed event is deleted and its change is lost from the read model, including during a temporary database outage.
claims.quote: public class SqsRetryableException extends RuntimeException {
claims.note: A grep of src/main finds SqsRetryableException only defined and checked for, never thrown. A later event for the same notification would still bring the record up to date.

claims.statement: Rejected messages are deleted rather than moved to a dead-letter queue by the service; the code calls this dead-lettering, but whether the queue has a dead-letter queue is not shown here.
claims.quote: Errors discarded as non-retryable (message deleted) ... // Then — non-retryable: message must be deleted from the queue (not redelivered)
claims.note: The ITs assert the queue empties; no DLQ is read or asserted.

claims.statement: Each received event is logged with its aggregate id, receive count and body length, and each applied event is logged with its aggregate id and version; the body itself is not logged.
